about: Every generated image in Blackwood Investigations. Run: node scripts/generate-art.mjs (see art/README.md). Prompts are built as style + kind + subject. Characters reuse the same description everywhere so they look like the same person.
style: Painted noir illustration in the manner of a 1980s paperback mystery cover and classic hand-painted point-and-click adventure game backgrounds. Gouache and oil textures with visible brushwork, warm tungsten lamplight against deep blue-black shadows, a muted palette of ochre, oxblood, bottle green, slate and nicotine cream, subtle film grain. Los Angeles, August 1985. Period-accurate details. The only readable words are the ones the subject spells out, printed exactly as written and correctly spelled; all other paperwork shows soft, unreadable typing or handwriting. No logos, brand names, watermarks or signatures.

background.suffix: A wide establishing interior view at standing eye level, composed for a 16:9 game screen, with depth and atmosphere. The room is empty of people. Keep the described empty surfaces and floor areas genuinely clear, because objects and people will be placed there separately.

portrait.suffix: A painted head-and-shoulders portrait, three-quarter view, looking slightly off to the side, softly lit from the upper left, against a dark, muted painted backdrop. Natural, believable face; not a caricature.

figure.suffix: The same person as the reference portrait, shown full length from head to toe, standing naturally, turned three-quarters toward the viewer, lit warmly from the upper left. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no floor, no backdrop, only a faint contact shadow at the feet.

sprite.suffix: A single isolated object, centered, entirely in frame, seen at a three-quarter angle from slightly above as it would sit in a room, lit warmly from the upper left to match a painted scene. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background with only a soft contact shadow; nothing else in the image.

evidence.suffix: A close-up evidence still life, raking lamplight, shallow depth of field, dark muted surroundings, the subject filling most of the frame.

site.suffix: A cinematic wide composition with room on the left third for page text, moody and atmospheric.

panorama.suffix: A wide side-on panorama, as seen through the side window of a moving car, composed for a 16:9 screen. The horizon runs level across the whole image and nothing important touches the left or right edge, so the image can repeat side by side. The bottom fifth is plain dark ground.

strip.suffix: Seen exactly side-on, lit by warm dusk and streetlight. Output a PNG with a truly transparent background (a real alpha channel, not a painted checkerboard pattern): nothing in the image except the subject.

pov.suffix: A cinematic first-person view at standing eye level, composed for a 16:9 screen, the way ahead leading into the picture. No people.

map.suffix: A hand-painted fold-out street map from the 1980s, seen flat from directly above and filling the whole image edge to edge like a sheet laid on a table: no table, no border, no frame. Muted period map colours: cream paper, ochre streets, sage green parkland, pale blue water, faint fold creases. Absolutely no words, letters, numbers, street names or symbols anywhere on the map.

face.suffix: An edit of the reference portrait: the same painting of the same person, at the same size, framing, pose, lighting, colors and brushwork. Change nothing except what the subject asks for. Do not move the head, change the expression elsewhere, or redraw the hair, clothing or background. Return one single image, never a sheet of several faces.

images.subject: Night view across a private investigator's desk in 1985 Los Angeles: venetian blinds throw stripes of streetlight over a fedora, a manila case folder and a glass of whiskey; beyond the window, city lights and palm-tree silhouettes against a deep blue sky.

A 1920s Spanish-revival house on a quiet Los Feliz street at night under a purple jacaranda tree, a single lamp lit in one window, a large dark sedan parked at the curb with its lights off, a streetlight casting a pool of amber light.

A private investigator's office on the eleventh floor of an older Wilshire Boulevard building at night, seen from a standing position just in front of a large dark wooden desk, looking slightly down onto it. The desk is close to the viewer and runs the full width of the lower part of the frame; its wide, flat top is clearly visible as a broad surface filling the bottom third of the image, completely clear and empty except a green banker's lamp at the far right end. Beyond the desk, an empty leather desk chair, and behind it a tall window with venetian blinds and city lights. On the left wall, a cork board with pinned papers, photographs and red string, above a filing cabinet. On the right wall, a large framed street map. At the far right, a small side table holding a black manual typewriter, and a coat stand with a trench coat and fedora. No people.

The living room of a widow's 1920s Spanish-revival house in Los Feliz, the quiet morning after a crime. Against the left wall, a roll-top writing desk with its top clear and one filing drawer pulled partly open. Left of center on the back wall, a solid oak front door. In the middle of the back wall, an arched doorway leading to a kitchen. On the right, a mahogany sideboard with a glass cake stand, stacked dessert plates and a two-thirds empty wine bottle. At the far right, a brick fireplace with a stand of fireplace tools. A chintz sofa on the left side of the floor. A patterned rug with a large open, clear area of floor in the center foreground. Faint police tape outlines on the carpet. No people.

The small, tidy kitchen of the same 1920s house, morning light. At center back, a window above a white enamel sink, the window open a few inches behind an aluminium insect screen. At the right, a wooden back door with a small window and a brass bolt. On the left wall, a pharmacy wall calendar and a beige wall telephone with a long coiled cord. Tiled counters with clear empty counter space to the left of the sink and beside it. At the far left edge, a doorway back to the living room.

A 24-hour diner on Sunset Boulevard at night in 1985. At the left, a red vinyl window booth with the night street and a pay phone visible outside. A long counter with chrome stools runs across the middle; behind the counter in the center is open, clear space where a waitress will stand. On the counter, a glass pie display case. At the right end of the counter, a cash register with clear counter space beside it. On the back wall near the kitchen pass, a pinned paper staff schedule. At the far right, a chrome 1950s jukebox. Warm neon glow.

A tidy bachelor apartment on the second floor of a Silver Lake building in 1985. At the left near the entry door, a clear empty stretch of wall and floor where a coat rack will stand. On the right, a modern desk with neat stacks of labelled client folders and a clear patch of desktop. A low coffee table in the center foreground with a clear top. Beige walls, venetian blinds, a framed abstract print, a kitchenette counter with clear space at the far right. A clear open area of floor in the center for a person to stand.

The front room of a retired schoolteacher's modest 1950s bungalow. At the left, a large front window with lace curtains looking across the street at a Spanish-revival house, a purple jacaranda tree and a streetlight. At the right, a wood console television set with rabbit-ear antennas, a reading armchair, bookshelves, and a clear patch of wall above the television for a framed photograph. A braided rug with clear open floor in the center for a person to stand and a clear spot near the front for a cat.

An independent auto repair garage in Atwater Village in 1985, daytime. Center right, an old pickup truck raised on a hydraulic lift with a drop light hanging under it. Along the left wall, a long tool bench with tools in labelled trays, a coffee can of bolts and a radio. On the right wall, a board of carbon-copy work orders on nails. Concrete floor with oil stains, an open roll-up bay door with daylight. A clear open area of floor at left of center for a mechanic to stand.

The loan department of a 1985 savings and loan office on Vermont Avenue, daytime. On the left wall, a row of steel four-drawer filing cabinets. A wooden desk at center right with a clear empty desktop, and a chair behind it with clear space for a person to stand. On the right wall, a cork notice board with rate sheets. Large windows with venetian blinds and daylight, beige and brown corporate decor, a potted plant.

Los Angeles at dusk in 1985, seen side-on from a boulevard: a long line of low hills with scattered house lights, the downtown towers small on the far horizon, a deep violet to amber sky with a few long clouds, and rows of low commercial buildings and apartment blocks in near-silhouette with warm lit windows. No cars, no people, no signs with lettering.

A long row of roadside silhouettes beside a Los Angeles boulevard: tall palm trees of different heights, two curved 1960s streetlights with warm glowing lamps, a low stucco wall and a few shrubs. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

A 1979 four-door American sedan in faded brown with chrome trim, seen exactly side-on in profile and facing right, headlights on and a warm glow from the dashboard, the silhouette of a man in a fedora at the wheel. Whole car in frame with space around it; only a faint contact shadow under the tyres.

Crossing Hollister Avenue in Los Feliz at night, looking straight across the quiet street: a row of 1920s Spanish-revival houses with red tile roofs and warm lit windows, a jacaranda tree in purple blossom under an amber streetlight, a few 1970s and 80s sedans parked along the curb, palm silhouettes against a deep blue sky, the asphalt and painted crosswalk leading toward the far curb.

Northeast Los Angeles in 1985. Across the top quarter, the green wooded hills of Griffith Park with a few winding park roads. The Los Angeles River, a pale blue channel with concrete banks, enters at the top just right of centre and curves down through the right third to the bottom right corner. A broad boulevard crosses the lower third from left to right. Everywhere else a dense grid of streets with small blocks of houses and tiny palm trees, a few larger avenues running north to south, and a small cluster of downtown towers drawn in the bottom right corner beside the river.

A quiet residential street in a small California coastal town at 3:40 in the morning, low fog drifting under palm trees. On the right, a small 1950s stucco house with a one-car garage, every window dark. At the curb in front of it, a dark full-size van with no windows down its side is pulling away with its headlights off, a faint wisp of exhaust in the cold air. Across the street, a single lit window where an old man's silhouette watches from behind the curtain. A streetlight at the far corner throws a pool of amber light onto the wet asphalt the van is about to pass through. The left third of the image is quiet dark fog and sky.

A dark radio station office high above Chicago on a rainy night in 1927. Through a tall window, Art Deco towers lit amber, the elevated train on its trestle, Model T cars on the wet street and a lit bridge over the river under a cloudy moon. Inside, on a polished desk, a gray fedora, a glass of whiskey, an ashtray, a pen on typed pages, a brass carbon microphone on its stand, a radio receiver with three glowing dials, headphones and a record turntable; a wall clock and a red ON AIR lamp glowing behind glass. The left third is the window and the city.

A small detective agency office in the Loop, Chicago, on a rainy morning in 1927. On the left wall a large cork board with pins and string, empty. Below it on a side table at the left, a black candlestick telephone. A heavy oak desk across the lower middle, its top clear except a green-shaded banker's lamp and a blotter. On the right wall a framed street map of Chicago. At the far right a wooden filing cabinet with a dictating machine on top, and a typewriter on a stand. A tall window behind the desk with rain on the glass and the elevated train beyond. A frosted glass door at the far right, lettered exactly: 'ASHBY & LOWE' on the first line and 'DETECTIVES' on the second.

A 1927 radio broadcasting studio, heavily hung with dark velvet drapes. A large window on the back wall into a control room, covered from this side by a drawn velvet curtain on a brass rod. An announcer's desk at the right with a green desk lamp and typed pages. In the middle of the carpet, a chalk outline and a scrubbed dark stain where a microphone floor stand used to stand. On the far right against the wall, a tall black amplifier rack on casters. On the left, a heavy oak door with two split iron brackets on its frame. A wall clock. Very still.

A 1927 radio station control room. A long control board of dials, brass keys and two inset turntables across the middle. A thick glass window above it into Studio A with a velvet curtain hanging on the far side. On the left wall a typed program schedule pinned up and a clockwork pen recorder in a glass case with a paper strip. A shelf with ledgers under the board. Warm tungsten light, a hum of equipment.

A cramped equipment storage room at the back of a radio station, 1927. Wooden crates of coiled black cable and spare tubes in straw at the lower left. A single bare bulb on a cord hanging from the ceiling. Low in the right-hand wall, a square painted panel with two small brass turn-buttons. A door with a bright new brass lock on the far right.

The front office of a 1927 radio station: a secretary's desk on the left with an Underwood typewriter and wire baskets of carbons, a wall shelf of green cloth ledgers behind it, and on the right, through an open glass-paneled door, the manager's private office with a big desk, a leather desk diary on the blotter and a small safe. Art Deco lamps, rain on the windows.

A small recording workshop at a 1927 radio station: a heavy disc-cutting lathe on a workbench in the middle, a wooden rack of twelve-inch aluminum discs in paper sleeves on the left wall, a ruled logbook chained to the bench on the right, coils of wire, a soldering iron, warm work lamps.

A Prohibition-era speakeasy in Chicago, 1927, behind a cigar store: a long dark wood bar on the left with crates stacked under a tablecloth behind it, a small bandstand under a blue paper lantern in the back middle with a piano, little tables with candles, smoke, and on the far right a half-open door to a back office with a desk.

A shut-up small bachelor apartment in Chicago, 1927, gloomy and dusty, the furniture covered here and there: a rolltop desk by a rain-streaked window on the right, a mantel with papers on it on the left, a door on the far left with a paper notice tacked inside it.

A comfortable Hyde Park parlor in 1927, afternoon light through lace curtains: an upright piano on the right with a framed photograph on top and a music stand, a sofa and an armchair, potted ferns, mourning crepe on a mirror, rain outside.

A 1920s Chicago police detective bureau squad room: rows of wooden desks with typewriters and candlestick telephones, a chalk blackboard on the left wall with case names, filing cabinets, a holding cell door at the far right, gray daylight through tall windows, cigarette smoke.

The gate and yard of a long brick river warehouse in Chicago in 1927, in gray daylight: a chain-link and iron gate, a watchman's shed, trucks and pallets in the yard, and the long warehouse running away toward the river with a painted sign on its end wall reading exactly: 'RIVERSIDE SHIPPING' on the first line and 'AND STORAGE CO.' on the second.

The front hall and parlor of a respectable Chicago rooming house in 1927: a front desk with a register book and a ring of keys on the left, a staircase, a parlor on the right with a baize card table and a cabinet radio, a lamp, rain outside.

A dark upper storeroom in a riverside warehouse at night, 1927: packing crates, one with a broken steel strap curling up, a box of manila shipping tags, a small window boarded over from outside with river lights through the gaps, a plank door to the stairs on the right, and a plank inner door with a cheap hasp and padlock in the middle. Lit only by moonlight through the gaps.

A cramped tally clerk's office upstairs in a riverside warehouse at night, 1927: a desk with a green cloth ledger open under a small lamp, a window over the black river with a bridge and its lamps beyond, a hand lamp with a shutter hanging on a hook by the window, a crate stenciled exactly 'BAY 6' at the top of a narrow stair going down on the right.

Inside a riverside warehouse bay at night, 1927: a wide plank door onto the river, barred with a heavy timber in iron brackets, crates stenciled 'RADIO CABINETS' stacked in the gloom, a narrow stair coming down on the left, river water gleaming under the door.

The Wells Street bridge over the Chicago River at night in 1927, seen from the walkway at the rail: across the black water, the long dark back of a brick warehouse with its river doors shut, two windows upstairs at the river end, one boarded and one a dark square of glass. Bridge lamps, rain, a streetcar's light passing.

The yard of a riverside warehouse at night in 1927, seen from just inside the gate: a watchman's shed with a lamp over it, pallets, and along the river side a row of plank river doors chained and padlocked, numbered in white paint. Headlights sweeping in from the street on the right.

Chicago in 1927, painted like a period street map. Lake Michigan in deep blue along the whole right edge. The Chicago River coming in from the lake just above center, then running west and splitting into north and south branches in a Y. South of the main river by the lake, the dense Loop with tiny Art Deco towers and the elevated train in a ring. North of the river, the Near North Side. Along the far left a long street running north to south. In the bottom right corner, a leafy neighborhood by the lake with a park. A street grid everywhere else, rail yards in the lower middle.

The bedroom of a small 1950s stucco house in a California coastal town, late afternoon light through a window on the left. A double bed in the middle with its sheets pulled off and heaped on the floor, a strip of gray tape stuck to the headboard. A nightstand on the right with a clock radio and a paperback, a dresser with a framed photograph further right, a doorway to the hall at the far right. The floor in front of the bed is clear. Nothing on the nightstand top except the clock radio and paperback.

A small 1950s kitchen and hall in a modest California house, afternoon. A Formica kitchen table with chairs on the left, its top clear; a beige wall telephone with a coiled cord on the left wall; a counter and drawers in the middle; a doorway to an attached garage on the right with a glimpse of a bicycle and trash cans; a narrow hall table near the front door at the far right, its top clear. A doorway to the bedroom at the far left. Clear floor space in the center.

A quiet residential street in a California coastal town on a gray afternoon, seen from the sidewalk. On the left, a small stucco house with a one-car garage and a narrow side path along a fence. Across the street in the middle distance, a modest house with a front porch and a porch chair. On the right, a streetlight on the corner. Palm trees and low fog. The curb and the asphalt in the foreground are clear except a dark oil stain.

Outside a small, isolated wooden cabin on a dirt road by a mountain lake, in late afternoon among tall pines. The cabin door in the center with a porch step; an oversized TV antenna on the roof; on the left side of the cabin, one window covered from inside with plywood; a woodpile at the far left; on the right, a full-size van completely covered by a brown tarp weighted with firewood. Pine needles on the ground; the ground in front of the door is clear.

Southern California in 1988. Along the left edge and the bottom, the Pacific coastline in pale blue: a small coastal town on the coast at the far left a third of the way down, and a harbor city on the bottom coast just right of center. A large city grid fills the center, slightly below the middle. To the right of the city, a broad valley of small towns. Across the top right corner, green pine-covered mountains with a small lake near the top right. Highways in ochre link the coast town, the city, the valley and the mountains.

A Benedictine abbey in a rain-dark Yorkshire dale at dusk, painted as a manuscript miniature: a squat bell tower against a gold-leaf sky, a cloister walk lit by one lamp, and in the foreground a small vaulted room whose oak door stands forced open, a single bronze candlestick missing from the ring of wax on the desk inside. Down the hillside a boy in a black novice's cloak wades a swollen beck toward a watermill. The left third of the image is quiet sky and moor.

The investigator's chamber in an abbey guest-house, 1327: whitewashed stone walls, a small hearth with a fire, a shuttered window on the upper left with rain on green glass looking out on a bell tower. Along the back wall a sturdy oak table cleared for laying out papers, with a ball of red thread on it; on the left a heavy oak door; on the right a tall wooden reading lectern by a candle stand; a narrow bed and a chest in the corner. A painted map of the dale hangs on the wall to the upper right. The tabletop and the floor in front of it are left clear.

A small vaulted stone book room off a cloister: an oak writing desk under a narrow window, ink spilled across an open great book on it, an iron-bound charter chest with its lid up on the right, a stool knocked over between them. On the left an oak door standing open on its hinges, its heavy swing bar down and an iron bracket hanging crooked from the wall beside it, and just below the bracket a small wooden cupboard door set into the wall. A ring of candle wax on the desk with nothing in it. The floor between desk and chest left clear.

A medieval scriptorium in a cloister walk: a row of wooden writing carrels facing open arches onto a rainy grass garth, sloping desks with quills, ink horns and parchment, a reading stand with an open book, wax tablets on a bench. Soft gray daylight. The middle floor left clear.

The interior of a Romanesque and early Gothic abbey church: two facing rows of oak choir stalls with small lamps, the high altar beyond, and on the left a small side altar under a painted Virgin with two bronze pricket candlesticks; on the right a low door to the sacristy with a board of writing hanging inside it. Candlelight and gold. The floor between the stalls left clear.

A medieval cloister on a rainy day: roofed stone walks on four sides around a square of wet grass with a stone well in the middle; on the left the west walk with an oak door and, a few paces along, a lower iron-banded door; on the right the arched entrance of the chapter house; a long stone bench along the near walk. The walk floor left clear.

A narrow vaulted stone passage lit by one candle: on the left wall halfway along, at chest height, a small wooden door set into the wall; a long iron hook hanging on a peg nearby; bundles of candles, a cask of lamp oil and rolled parchment along the right wall; low oak doors at each end. Damp stone, close and dark. The floor left clear.

An abbot's private chamber: a good fire in a hooded fireplace on the left with a small carved seated saint on the mantel, a carved oak chair, a table on the left of center with a long parchment roll half unwound and weighted with an inkpot, a side table with sealed letters on the right, a crucifix, a window of small panes. Warm and comfortable. The floor in front of the table left clear.

The kitchen court of an abbey's cellarer's range: a muddy cobbled court in rain with a lamp over a door; on the left a little office with tally sticks and a peg with a black habit on it, a desk with a ledger; beyond, the vaulted cellar with casks; in the corner a low iron-banded door; on the right the lit doorway and window of a guest kitchen with a fire inside; a salt store with a wooden bin. The court floor in the middle left clear.

An abbey gatehouse: a stone archway with two great oak gate leaves and a wicket, a porter's window with a board and a long parchment roll beside it, rain on the cobbles, the precinct wall running off either side, the moor road beyond. The ground in front of the window left clear.

A small medieval watermill at Hollin Bridge beside a swollen brown beck: a turning wooden wheel on the right, the mill house of stone and timber with its door open, sacks of grain, a ladder up to a loft on the left, alder trees, rain. The yard in front of the door left clear.

The hall of a medieval manor house: a long timber-roofed hall with a fire burning on a central hearth, a hound asleep by it, the lord's table on a dais, painted heraldic shields on the wall, an open door to a yard where hedge stakes are stacked. The floor between the hearth and the dais left clear.

A small locked record room above a chapter house: iron-bound chests along the walls, a shallow drawer of wax seal impressions pulled out on the left, a thick book open on a stand, an oak door with three keyholes. Dusty light from one narrow window. The floor left clear.

A medieval monastic infirmary: a long whitewashed room, a body laid out under a linen sheet on a board with candles at head and foot on the left, an old monk asleep under blankets on a bed on the right, a small fire, shelves of pots and herbs. Quiet and gentle. The floor in the middle left clear.

The inside of a medieval bell tower: heavy oak bell frame and beams, a great bronze bell above, a new pale rope hanging beside an old frayed rope coiled on the floor, a thick book chained to a shelf on the left, wind through the louvers, a gap behind one beam on the right. The floor left clear.

images.subject: A Yorkshire dale in 1327. In the upper middle an abbey church with a bell tower; just below it a square cloister with buildings around it (chapter house and infirmary to the right of the cloister, the cellarer's range and a kitchen court to its left, an abbot's lodging below right); a guest-house and a gatehouse in the wall at lower left; a precinct wall around it all. A beck flows from the top right down the right side, with a small watermill on it at the right a little below the middle. A manor house with a hall on the moor in the upper right. Brown moorland, green fields, a road from the gate down the lower left.

A muddy track across a rain-dark Yorkshire moor in 1327, painted as a manuscript miniature, looking ahead: stone walls, sheep, the abbey's bell tower in the valley below, a gold-leaf sky with stylized clouds, a footbridge over a swollen beck in the distance. No people.

A quiet street of brick row houses in a small western Pennsylvania steel town on a rainy autumn night in 2018. On the right, a large oak at the curb with a pale fresh gash in its bark at bumper height; at its foot, a small roadside memorial of glass candle jars glowing in the rain, a few wilted flowers and a child's stuffed rabbit. Across the street, one brick house with its porch light on and a woman in a cardigan standing alone on the top step, half in shadow, looking down the street. Far down the block, at the corner under a sodium-orange streetlight, the red taillights of a dark full-size SUV turning away, a tiny amber glow inside its dashboard. Wet asphalt reflecting the candles and the streetlight, steam rising from a storm drain, smokestacks of an old mill faint against the clouded sky. The left third of the image is quiet dark rain, brick and sky.

A small private investigator's field office on the eleventh floor of an old downtown Pittsburgh building on a rainy afternoon in October 2018. A cork board on the left wall, its surface bare. A tall window in the center of the back wall looking out on rain, bridges and the gray Monongahela River. A large framed street map on the right wall. A broad wooden desk across the whole foreground, its top clear except for a lamp at the far right, with a desk phone at the far left. Radiator under the window, a coat on a hook, warm lamplight against the gray daylight.

A quiet street of brick row houses in a small western Pennsylvania steel town on a gray, wet October afternoon in 2018. In the left-center foreground, a large oak at the curb with a pale scar in its bark at bumper height; at its foot, a small memorial of glass candle jars, wilted flowers and a stuffed rabbit, and a hedge with leaf litter in its roots just right of the tree. Across the street on the right, a brick house with a porch and front steps, its front door at the top of the steps. Further right, the road bends out of sight behind a tall, thick privet hedge. Wet asphalt with faint black skid marks running toward the tree. Old mill stacks faint in the clouded sky.

The front hall and living room of a comfortable older brick house in the evening, 2018, seen from inside. The front door at the left, closed, with a window beside it at the far left showing the dark street. A small hall table with a ceramic lamp beside the door. A television in a low cabinet at the left. A dining table in the center with a closed laptop on it, a doorway through to a kitchen on the right with a school district calendar on the fridge and a small kitchen table. Stairs at the back right with framed school staff photos up the wall. Warm lamplight, a lived-in, orderly home. Clear floor space in the center.

The same front hall and living room of the older brick house at night, 2018, the same view and layout as before, but something has happened. The front door at the left stands open about a foot, the porch light on outside and rain beyond it. The ceramic hall lamp lies on its side on the hall runner, its shade crushed. A pair of reading glasses on a beaded chain lies on the runner near the stairs, one arm bent. A dark smear on the door frame at shoulder height. The television is still on, its screen glowing blue in the cabinet at the left. On the dining table in the center, a laptop sits open, its screen lit. A composition notebook lies open beside a cold mug on the kitchen table on the right. Nobody is there. Cold air, dim lamplight, an unsettling stillness.

The detective bureau of a small-city police department in 2018. A cork case board on the left wall covered in pinned photos and a street map. Desks with computer monitors and stacks of binders, one cluttered desk in the right foreground. Behind it, a window with half-open blinds looking out over an impound lot where a silver SUV sits under a blue tarp. At the back right, the glass window of an interview room. Fluorescent light, gray-blue walls, a coffee machine. Clear floor space in the center.

Inside a small gas station convenience store at night, 2018, seen from the customer side. A counter with a register in the center, a rack of cigarettes and lottery tickets on the wall behind it, a doorway to a back office on the right with a security monitor glowing inside, split into four camera views. Large front windows on the left looking out on the fuel pumps under a bright canopy, and beyond them a dark strip of parking lot by a dumpster. Refrigerated drink cases, wet floor mats, fluorescent light. The space behind the counter is clear.

The living room of a modest family house in a Pennsylvania town on a rainy afternoon, 2018, a little too quiet. A window on the left looking out on a small wet yard with a swing set. A shelf at the far left with framed photos. Through a doorway in the back, a kitchen with children's crayon drawings on the fridge. A cardboard box on the floor at the right with work boots and a mug in it. A small hall desk with drawers at the far right by the front door. A sofa with a child's blanket. Clear floor space in the center.

The office of a small real estate development company in a renovated brick industrial building, 2018. Exposed brick, polished concrete floor, steel windows. A large framed architect's rendering of new riverside townhouses on the back wall. A conference table in the right-center foreground with a thick binder on it. A bookkeeper's desk with a computer at the far left, a wire invoice tray beside it. A low wooden credenza with a drawer at the right. Cool daylight, clean and modern. Clear floor space in the center.

The garage of a small private security company on a rainy day, 2018. Two vehicle bays with a concrete floor; the second bay, in the center-right, is empty, with an oil stain on the concrete. A whiteboard with a fleet list and a printed duty roster on the left wall. A workbench with tools along the left. At the right, an open door into a small office with filing cabinets, and a fridge just inside it covered in magnets and menus. Ceiling bay fans, rain on a metal roof, gray light through high windows. A company logo sign on the back wall reading exactly: BELL SECURITY SERVICES.

A tow truck yard beside a highway in western Pennsylvania on a gray, rainy day, 2018. A flatbed tow truck parked on the left with a GPS antenna on the cab roof. Gravel, puddles, chain-link fencing, a stack of tires. On the right, a small office trailer with its door open, a desk and a laptop visible inside, and a sheet of paper pinned to the trailer wall beside the door. Highway traffic blurred beyond the fence. Clear gravel in the center.

A municipal records annex in an old brick civic building, 2018. A public computer terminal on a small desk at the left with a label on the monitor frame. A wooden counter with a visitor sign-in book on it. A long table in the center with a cardboard records box on it. A wide steel flat-file map cabinet with shallow drawers at the center-right. At the right, a doorway and stairs leading down to a basement archive, dimly lit. Rows of shelves with archive boxes, fluorescent light, rain on a tall window.

A dead-end gravel access road in an old riverfront industrial district, overcast morning after rain, 2018. In the center, a dark gray Ford Explorer SUV with partly burned, soot-blackened rear windows parked beside a rusted rail spur, inside a square of yellow police tape on poles. At the far left, a tall pole on a scrapyard's chain-link fence with a security camera on top, pointing toward the road. Across an empty field on the right, a white construction-site office trailer with a dumpster behind it, and beyond it the gray river. Puddles, weeds, crows, a distant freight train.

A clean, modern county forensic laboratory, 2018. Tall steel evidence lockers on the left with case numbers on tape. A long lab bench on the right with a comparison microscope, evidence bags in neat rows and a label printer, a whiteboard above it covered in soft, unreadable notes. Fume hoods, white cabinets, cool fluorescent light. Clear floor space in the center.

A dark gray 2016 Ford Explorer SUV seen from the rear three-quarter angle, with a black roof rack and a small amber strobe light on the left of the dashboard visible through the windshield. On the rear hatch, white vinyl lettering reading exactly, on two lines: BELL SECURITY / UNIT 4. The black plastic trim on the right front wheel arch looks newer than the rest.

A modern black smartphone lying at a slight angle, its screen lit with a soft, unreadable home screen.

Bellwether, a small fictional steel town on a river in western Pennsylvania in 2018, and the edge of Pittsburgh. A broad pale blue river enters at the top right corner, where a dense city grid sits, and curves down the right side to the bottom right. Along its near bank in the lower right, an old industrial riverfront of rail lines and empty lots. The town's small downtown grid sits just above the center. Residential streets of small blocks spread across the left and center, with a cul-de-sac neighborhood a little below the center right. A highway in ochre runs from the lower left corner up toward the center. A road runs from the downtown to a county complex in the upper right. Green hillsides and parkland fill the gaps.

images.subject: Bellwether at dusk in October 2018, seen side-on from a riverside road: the wide gray river in the middle distance, steep wooded hills beyond it with scattered house lights, an old steel mill's smokestacks and a steel truss bridge, rows of brick row houses climbing the hillside in near-silhouette with warm lit windows, a slate gray to rust-orange sky with low clouds after rain. No cars, no people, no signs with lettering.

A long row of roadside silhouettes beside a small-town Pennsylvania street: bare and half-bare autumn maple trees, two modern cobra-head streetlights with sodium-orange lamps on wooden utility poles strung with wires, a stretch of chain-link fence and a short guardrail. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

A dark blue 2015 four-door midsize sedan, seen exactly side-on in profile and facing right, headlights on, rain beading on the paint, the silhouette of a driver at the wheel lit faintly by a phone mounted on the dashboard. Whole car in frame with space around it; only a faint contact shadow under the tires.

Walking along a wet sidewalk on a quiet street of brick row houses in a small western Pennsylvania steel town at dusk in October 2018, looking straight ahead: porches with lit windows, maple trees dropping orange leaves, cars from the 2010s parked at the curb, sodium-orange streetlights coming on, puddles reflecting the light, old mill stacks faint above the rooftops. No people.

A police crime scene photo board: three glossy color photographs pinned side by side, a silver Honda CR-V against an oak tree at night with its airbags deployed, bullet holes along its driver's side, and a dent with dark gray paint streaks on its rear quarter panel, above a hand-drawn scene diagram with soft, unreadable notes.
A preliminary autopsy report on a county medical examiner's letterhead, two stapled pages on a steel desk, soft unreadable typed text, a paper clip and a pen.
A small thermal-paper gas station receipt lying on a counter, curling slightly, soft unreadable print, with handwriting in blue pen on the back showing through faintly.

A computer monitor in a dim back office showing a grainy color still from a gas station security camera at night: fuel pumps under a bright canopy, a silver SUV at a pump, and at the dark far edge of the lot a dark full-size SUV with a tiny amber light glowing on its dashboard. A timestamp in the corner reading exactly: 09/14/2018 21:52:02.

A curved piece of black textured plastic vehicle wheel-arch trim about six inches long, with two broken mounting clips, flecks of dark gray paint along one edge and a smear of silver paint on the other, lying in an evidence bag on a lab table beside a ruler.

A police evidence tray holding spent brass cartridge cases in two separate groups, seven on the left and five on the right, each beside a small numbered yellow marker, with a typed report beside the tray in soft, unreadable text.

A photograph looking across a residential street from a brick house's front steps at eye level: an oak tree with candles at its foot under a streetlight in plain view, and to the right a tall privet hedge hiding the street beyond a bend.

A police property inventory form on a clipboard with soft, unreadable typed lines and a handwritten note at the bottom, beside two wallets, two phones, a set of keys and a carnival wristband in clear plastic evidence bags.
A small spiral pocket notepad with a company logo, lying open, its last pages covered in hurried ballpoint handwriting, soft and unreadable except for one underlined word reading exactly: ORANGE.
The first page of an environmental assessment report on consultant letterhead, with a red RECEIVED rubber stamp, soft unreadable typed text and a data table with one row circled in red ink.

An environmental assessment report page in a three-ring binder with a colored tab, soft unreadable typed text, the lower paragraphs in a very slightly different typeface and spacing from the rest of the page.

Pages from a surveyor's field book: columns of handwritten coordinates and a pencil sketch of a building outline with six small circles marked around it and one inside it, a north arrow and wavy lines for a river.
A printed accounts payable ledger page on a desk, columns of soft unreadable payments, with a pencil question mark in the margin next to one line.
A single printed invoice on a security company's letterhead, mostly empty space, a single line item and a total in soft unreadable type, lying in a wire tray on top of other invoices.

A brown nine-by-twelve envelope, opened, with RACHEL handwritten on the front in marker; spilling out of it, photocopied report pages, a handwritten note on notepaper and a small black USB flash drive.
A computer printout of a document history log with soft unreadable rows, paper-clipped to a photocopy of a handwritten visitor sign-in book page and a small handwritten sticky note.
A paper wall calendar pinned to a refrigerator door, turned to October, with a photo of a high school marching band at the top and handwriting in a few of the date squares, soft and unreadable.

A black and white marbled composition notebook lying open on a kitchen table beside a mug, its page covered in neat handwriting, soft and unreadable, with a small sketch of a car's dashboard and a circled number 4.

Southern California at dusk in October 1988, seen side-on from a freeway: low brown hills with scattered house lights, a long line of tract houses and low commercial buildings in near-silhouette with warm lit windows, a few oil pumpjacks on a ridge, a deep violet to amber sky with long thin clouds. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

Los Angeles at dusk in October 1988, seen side-on from Wilshire Boulevard: a row of 1960s and 1980s office towers with lit windows, the downtown towers on the far horizon, palm silhouettes, a deep violet to amber sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A small foggy California beach town at dusk in October 1988, seen side-on from the coast road: the ocean and a long wooden pier on the horizon, low fog drifting in, rows of small 1950s stucco houses with warm lit windows, palms, a lifeguard tower on the sand. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

Long Beach at dusk in October 1988, seen side-on from the harbor freeway: the port with tall container cranes, an old ocean liner moored in the distance, palm-lined apartment blocks with lit windows, the bay and a deep violet to amber sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

The San Bernardino Mountains in late afternoon in October 1988, seen side-on from a winding mountain highway: steep slopes of tall dark pines, granite outcrops, a glimpse of a blue lake far below with a few cabin lights, golden light low across the ridges and a cool pale sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A quiet San Gabriel Valley suburb at night in November 1988, seen side-on from a boulevard: rows of ranch houses with porch lights, sycamores and oaks, a strip of shops with dim lights, and the dark San Gabriel Mountains on the horizon under a cool moonlit sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A long row of roadside silhouettes beside a Southern California road in 1988: tall palm trees of different heights, two tall 1980s cobra-head streetlights with warm glowing lamps, a low cinderblock wall, oleander shrubs. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

A long row of roadside silhouettes beside a mountain highway: tall dark ponderosa pines of different heights, a low wooden guardrail with weathered posts, a granite boulder and a few manzanita shrubs. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

Walking along a quiet residential street in a small California beach town at night in October 1988, looking down the sidewalk: small 1950s stucco houses with one-car garages and warm lit windows, palms and a jacaranda, low fog drifting under an amber streetlight, a few 1980s sedans and a pickup parked along the curb, the glow of the harbor boulevard at the end of the street.

Walking along a narrow lakeshore road at dusk in the San Bernardino Mountains in October 1988, looking ahead: tall pines on both sides, small wooden cabins with lit windows among the trees, the dark lake glimpsed through the trunks on the right, pine needles on the cracked asphalt, the warm light of a small general store far ahead.

Pittsburgh at dusk on a rainy evening in October 2018, seen side-on from a riverside parkway: the river with yellow steel bridges, the downtown skyline lit up, the steep wooded bluff of Mount Washington, low rain clouds glowing orange. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

The small downtown of a western Pennsylvania steel town on a rainy October evening in 2018, seen side-on: three- and four-story brick commercial blocks with lit shop windows, a stone courthouse with a clock tower, wet sodium-orange streetlights, the river bridge beyond. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A commercial strip highway outside a western Pennsylvania town on a rainy October evening in 2018, seen side-on: a tow yard behind chain-link, a gas station canopy glowing, used car lots, fast-food pole signs with no lettering, wooded hills behind under low clouds. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A riverfront in a western Pennsylvania steel town on a rainy October evening in 2018, seen side-on: a rail spur and rusting freight cars, a coal barge on the wide gray river, the steel truss bridge, a gravel access road and the dark shapes of the old mill. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

Rolling wooded hills of western Pennsylvania on a rainy October evening in 2018, seen side-on from a county highway: autumn trees in rust and gold, a farm with a red barn, a low modern government building with lit windows on a hilltop, low rain clouds. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

Walking along a street of brick row houses in a western Pennsylvania steel town on a rainy October night in 2018, looking down the sidewalk: porch lights, steep front steps, wet cars from the 2010s parked along the curb, a large oak at the curb, a small corner convenience store glowing at the end of the block, sodium-orange streetlights reflecting in the puddles.

Walking along the main street of a small western Pennsylvania steel-town downtown on a rainy October evening in 2018, looking ahead: brick commercial blocks with lit shop windows, a stone courthouse with a clock tower at the end of the street, wet sidewalks, parked 2010s cars, sodium-orange streetlights.

Chicago at dusk on a rainy evening in October 1927, seen side-on from a street: Art Deco and Beaux-Arts towers with lit windows, the elevated train crossing on its steel trestle, the river with a lit bascule bridge, soot and smoke in a deep amber and slate sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

The Chicago River at night in October 1927, seen side-on from a riverside street: brick warehouses with loading doors on the water, a raised bascule bridge with its lamps lit, a tugboat, fog over the black water and the city towers beyond. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

Hyde Park on Chicago's South Side at dusk in October 1927, seen side-on from a boulevard: stately greystone houses and brick apartment buildings with lit windows, tall elms losing their leaves, the Gothic towers of a university in the distance, a deep amber sky. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

South Halsted Street in Chicago at night in October 1927, seen side-on: crowded brick tenements with lit windows above small shops, a streetcar line, market awnings, smoke from chimneys and the glow of the stockyards on the horizon. No people, no cars, no signs with lettering.

A long row of street silhouettes beside a Chicago street in 1927: the steel columns and girders of the elevated train, cast-iron lamp posts with glowing globes, a fire hydrant and a newsstand with no lettering. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

A 1926 black four-door Packard sedan with chrome headlamps, running boards and spoked wheels, the silhouette of a man in a fedora at the wheel. Seen exactly side-on in profile and facing right, headlights on and a warm glow from the dashboard. Whole car in frame with space around it; only a faint contact shadow under the tyres.

Walking down a long Art Deco corridor on the 19th floor of a Chicago radio station in October 1927, looking ahead: polished terrazzo floor, brass wall sconces, studio doors with frosted glass windows, a red lamp lit over the far studio door, velvet curtains, the city lights through a window at the end.

Walking along a rainy Chicago Loop street at night in October 1927, looking ahead: tall office buildings with lit windows, the elevated train on its trestle overhead, a streetcar and Model T cars on the wet street, glowing lamp posts.

Walking along North Clark Street in Chicago at night in October 1927, looking ahead: a cigar store with a warm lit window, brick walk-up apartments, a speakeasy's dim doorway in a side alley, wet cobbles and streetcar tracks, glowing lamp posts, Model T cars parked along the curb.

Walking along a riverside street of warehouses in Chicago at night in October 1927, looking ahead: brick warehouses with loading doors, wet cobbles and rail tracks, fog off the river, the lit iron bascule bridge at the end of the street, a single lamp over a night gate.

The abandoned East Mill of a steel works on a river at dusk in the rain, a chain-link gate with police tape in the foreground, one brick maintenance building inside with a single work light glowing in a ground-floor window. A young woman's faded 1996 senior portrait is taped to the gate. The left third of the image is quiet gray sky and river mist.

Hollow Creek, a small fictional steel town on the Monongahela River in western Pennsylvania, in 2018. A broad brown river runs across the lower right; along its near bank the long rusted sheds of a closed steel works, its West End near the center bottom and its East Mill toward the right. The town's small downtown grid sits just left of center, with brick row-house streets around it and a hillside of houses above. A county highway in ochre runs from the upper left; a dirt road climbs into wooded ridges at the bottom left. Painted as a hand-drawn local map with no readable labels.

A two-room private investigator's field office above a small-town hardware store: tall rain-streaked window over a main street on the upper middle, a large cork case board on the left wall, a second wall space beside it with two long strips of paper pinned up for timelines, a wooden desk across the lower middle with a laptop and a desk lamp, a light table on the right, a mail slot and wire in-tray by the door on the far right. Desk surface left clear.

The East Gate of a closed steel mill on a rural road in the rain: a chained double chain-link gate on rusted posts with police tape woven through it, a gravel shoulder on the lower left, inside the fence a dark two-story brick maintenance building, a break in the chain-link to the right. A road runs back left toward a distant small store sign over the trees.

The ground floor of an abandoned brick maintenance building in a steel mill: a heavy steel workbench with an angle-iron edge and a vise against the left brick wall with drifts of copper wire shavings beneath it, a fixed steel ladder to a loft on the far left, a steel mesh cage wall with a steel door in the middle right, an open doorway to the outside on the right. Gray daylight through broken high windows.

Inside a small windowless tool room in an abandoned mill: steel mesh walls on three sides, a brick wall at the back with empty steel shelving, a bare concrete floor swept clean, police scene photographs pinned to the mesh on the left, harsh flashlight and work-light glare.

The abandoned second-floor general manager's office of a steel mill administration building: water-stained ceiling tiles, a big window looking out over rusted furnace sheds, a row of soft damp cardboard records cartons along the floor in the lower half, an empty executive desk.

An abandoned steel mill maintenance office: a shelf of green bound ledgers on the left, a cluttered steel desk in the center with a three-ring binder on it, a framed crew photograph on the right wall, pipes along the ceiling, dust and gray light.

A rusted steel mill loading yard in the rain behind a furnace shed: rail tracks, puddles, a square steel hatch in the concrete in the middle with a ladder going down into darkness, faded plastic flowers wired to the hatch rail.

The upstairs bedroom of a modest steel-town house kept as it was in 1996: a single bed with a cardboard box of keepsakes on it, a 1996 wall calendar on the left wall, framed family photographs on the right wall, posters of 1990s bands, a desk, rain at the window. A woman's figure will stand in the middle; the middle floor left clear.

A small-town auto repair shop interior: a lift with a car on it in the back, a counter and register on the right with a metal work order rack beside it, a framed old photograph behind the register, stairs up to a loft on the left with bound books on shelves, an old red portable welder on a back shelf. The middle floor left clear for a figure.

A small-town police detectives' room: two cluttered desks, a corkboard on the right wall, a long table by the window on the lower left with old manila case folders laid out on it, an interview room door with a window on the right. The middle floor left clear for a figure.

A county medical examiner's anthropology lab: a glowing light box on the left wall with x-ray films, a steel exam table under a white sheet on the right, cabinets, clean cold light. The middle left clear for a figure.

A small-town newspaper newsroom: a few desks with computers, stacks of papers, a reference shelf of fat old telephone directories on the left by a window, bound volumes of old newspapers on the right. The middle left clear for a figure.
A municipal building basement records room: gray steel filing cabinets, a long table under a hanging fluorescent light with a thin file folder laid open on it, an index card box.
A county archive room: rows of gray document boxes on steel shelving, a worktable with an open binder and a folder of photographs, fluorescent light.

An old union hall: wood paneling, a bar at the back, card tables, a tall steel grievance file cabinet on the left, a wall of framed memorial photographs on the right, a television on a bracket. The middle floor left clear for two figures.

A retired man's small brick house, seen from inside the front room: a den with mounted bass on the wall and a recliner, a desk with a blotter on the lower left, a kitchen beyond with a calendar on the refrigerator on the right, a bedroom doorway with a nightstand on the far right. The middle left clear.

A self storage facility row on a gray morning: a roll-up unit door half raised with metal shelving and spilled file boxes inside, a police photo board on an easel by the door, evidence markers on the concrete; to the right a small office with a terminal and a filing cabinet visible through its window.

The reception area of a developer's office in a restored old bank building: marble floor, a framed letter on the left wall, a large framed watercolor rendering of riverfront apartments on the right wall, leather chairs, warm lamplight. The middle left clear for a figure.

A small security company office in a cinderblock building by railroad tracks: a framed license and roster on the left wall, a metal desk with a green ledger on it, radios charging, a window onto a gravel lot. The middle left clear for a figure.

Inside the front hall and through to the kitchen of a tidy brick ranch house: a coat rack with a coat and cap, a hall runner rug, a dining table with papers on it in the middle, a kitchen counter with a coffee maker on the left, a neighbor's front door visible through a window on the right.
A muddy dirt road in wooded ridges before dawn: a rusted pipe gate across the road with a chain, police cruisers with lights off behind, flashlight beams, bare trees, the road climbing into darkness.

The main room of a rough two-room hunting cabin: paneled walls, a cold wood stove with a shelf above it, a table with a lantern, antlers over the door, an open trap door in the floor in the lower middle.
An abandoned steel mill first-aid room: a stretcher, a glass-fronted oxygen cabinet on the right, a shelf of bound logbooks on the left, peeling paint, gray light.
An old small-town photo and frame shop: frame samples on the walls, a counter, a back-room filing cabinet visible on the left, a narrow darkroom door with a red light above it on the right.
A modest kitchen in a small-town house: a refrigerator covered in photos and a child's soccer schedule, a kitchen table, rain at the window. The middle left clear for a figure.
A small-town basement rec room: wood paneling, a sofa, a table, shelves of shoeboxes, a furnace in the corner. The middle left clear for a figure.

The old main gate of a steel works by a wide brown river in the rain: a small concrete guardhouse, a white construction site trailer to the left, a concrete boat ramp running down into the river on the right.
A county recorder of deeds office: ceiling-high shelves of red deed books on the left, a long wooden counter, brass lamps, a tall window. The middle left clear for a figure.

An abandoned rail service building used as a scrap yard weigh office: a big platform scale on the floor, a weigh office counter with oversized ledgers on it, a window with an old scale beam, hand-painted signs on the wall, gray light through broken panes.

The same abandoned mill maintenance building ground floor lit up by police work lights on tripods: the steel workbench ringed with yellow tape, yellow tape running along the floor to a steel mesh cage door, the loft ladder cleared with a police officer's flashlight shining up into the loft.
A yellowed 1996 police missing person form on a desk, typed in a typewriter font, a school photo of a young dark-haired woman clipped to the corner, under a desk lamp.

A spiral notebook with a worn cardboard cover lying open on a bedspread, blue ballpoint handwriting, one page torn out at the binding.
A 1996 bank wall calendar turned to August, river photograph above the grid, handwriting in some squares, one square written in hard pressed ink.
A punched paper time card and a small spiral darkroom log on a darkroom counter under a red safelight, trays and a copy stand behind.
Two black and white 8x10 photographic prints of a typed office memo, with a handwritten note at the bottom, half out of an orange photo studio envelope.
Photocopied yellow legal pad pages of a detective's slanting handwritten notes, clipped together in a manila folder.

A rusted steel door hasp with a broken short weld bead, a heavy chain through the handle held by an old brass padlock rusted shut, wooden pallets leaning nearby, police evidence tags.

A worn women's denim jacket laid on a steel exam table beside a gold high school class ring with a red stone, a brass key on a paper tag, folded newspaper clipping and a few dollar bills, evidence bags.

Two dental x-ray films side by side on a light box with a report form beneath.

A typed shift roster with a tool room sign-out sheet clipped behind it.

A government inspection summary with a federal seal header on a gray archive table under fluorescent light.
Handwritten statements on union letterhead, a pencil and an old cassette recorder beside them.
A photographic contact sheet and enlargements of a dim industrial gas valve room: a large fan motor with a red danger tag wired to it, a wall monitor panel with a dark display.
A narrow underground valve gallery under a steel furnace, rusted valves in a row, three wall sensor heads, a seized fan with a scrap of red tag, a brass memorial plate on the rail, flashlight beam.
Typed 1996 meeting minutes on letterhead, initialed, in a manila folder labeled for the general manager's office.
A single folded ledger page with handwritten entries and a small handwritten slip clipped to it, lying in the hidden compartment of a green metal tackle box.
A banded stack of identical printed safety bulletins in an open steel desk drawer, a faded sticky note on top.
A confidential executive bonus schedule page with a payroll PAID stamp, in an HR file folder.
A thick recorded real estate agreement in a deed book binder, a clause flagged with a paper strip.
Two letters in a borough file folder: a union letterhead letter with a RECEIVED stamp and a short typed borough reply.
A typed question and answer interview summary in a government binder.
A short typed borough memorandum on letterhead, signed, in the same file folder.
A bound medical treatment logbook open to handwritten entries, an oxygen mask and an old stretcher in a dim first aid room.
A labeled audio cassette and a portable cassette player on a newsroom desk piled with clippings.
A 2018 desk answering machine with a blinking message light on a cluttered office desk.
A hardware store wall calendar on a refrigerator door, handwritten notes in several squares, magnets.

An autopsy summary report on a clipboard on a steel counter, gloves and a pen.
A dot-matrix style printout of a gate access log with time-stamped rows, on a storage facility office counter.

A stack of printed phone call detail records with a few lines highlighted in yellow.

A private investigator's office at night, lit by one green-shaded desk lamp. In the middle-right of the frame stands a large cork board on a wheeled black metal frame with casters, covered in pinned documents, photographs, receipts and index cards, joined by red string into six separate clusters that all run toward one empty spot in the center of the board where a single pushpin holds nothing. On the desk in front of it, a small scattered pile of old tarnished silver coins catches the lamplight. Rain streaks a tall window behind, with the faint lights of a city. The left third of the image is quiet dark office wall and shadow. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A small-town Pennsylvania nonprofit's office on a rainy November night, seen through a second-floor window of an old brick building. Inside, one desk lamp is still on. The desk is in disarray: a drawer pulled out and forced, papers scattered on the floor, a filing cabinet hanging open, and a clean empty rectangle in the dust on the desk where a heavy ornament used to sit. On a bookshelf behind, one thick old accounting reference book sits slightly out of line with the others. Below the window, in the wet rear parking lot, a service door stands ajar and a plain white contractor's van idles with its lights off. The left third of the image is quiet dark brick and rain. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

The sixth-floor corridor of an upscale Washington, D.C. hotel late at night, patterned carpet and brass wall sconces. In the middle-right, a guest room door stands open a few inches, warm light spilling out; through the gap you can see a suitcase still zipped on a luggage rack and a smartphone glowing face-up on a bedside table. The brass room number on the door reads exactly "614", printed exactly as written. At the far end of the corridor, a plain gray service door is propped open with a rubber wedge, a dim service elevator beyond. The left third of the image is quiet dark corridor wall and shadow. No people. The only readable text is "614". Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A Baltimore shipping container terminal at night in harbor fog. Towering gantry cranes fade into the mist above stacks of rust-red, blue and gray containers lit by sodium-orange floodlights. In the middle-right, in a narrow lane between two container stacks, a yellow hard hat lies upturned on the wet asphalt beside a tipped-over clipboard, and a heavy steel cargo bar leans against a container wall. One container door at the end of the lane stands slightly open, a sliver of light inside. The left third of the image is quiet fog, dark water and distant crane lights. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A quiet cafe in Old Town Alexandria, Virginia, on a gray December morning. In the middle-right, a small window table set for two: one coffee cup half drunk, the other full and untouched, gone cold. Tucked under the sugar dispenser is a folded scrap of paper with one line handwritten in blue ink: "You're looking at the wrong people." printed exactly as written. Through the rain-streaked window, a cobbled brick street, and far down it a woman in a dark coat walks away carrying a small travel bag, too distant to make out. The left third of the image is quiet window, rain and brick. The only readable text is the handwritten note. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A private conference room off the ballroom of a grand Manhattan hotel during a charity gala in December. In the middle-right, a polished table with one chair knocked over, a glass of whiskey still standing, papers spilled across the carpet, and a bare spot on the table where a heavy marble desk piece used to sit. Through a half-open double door behind, the ballroom glows gold: crystal chandeliers, round tables in white linen, guests in evening dress as soft silhouettes, a distant podium. Snow falls past a tall window onto Manhattan lights. The left third of the image is quiet dark paneled wall. No identifiable faces. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

The inside of a corporate records archive the morning after a fire, late December. Long rows of metal shelving blackened by smoke, cardboard file boxes charred and collapsed, ash on the concrete floor, pale winter sunlight cutting through haze from a broken high window with snow on the sill. In the middle-right, one shelf stands untouched by the fire, and on it a single clean gap where one box was taken away before the flames, its dust outline still visible. The left third of the image is quiet smoke and shadow. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A freestanding cork board on a wheeled frame, seen straight on: a brushed steel frame with bolted corners, two upright legs ending in black rubber casters, the cork a paler, cooler tan than an office wall board. A few pushpins and one short loop of red string on an otherwise bare surface, so whatever the player pins later reads clearly. No readable text.
