The reception area of a small community foundation on the second floor of a 1912 brick office building in a small western Pennsylvania county seat, a gray November day in 2018. On the left, a tall window onto a main street of brick storefronts, with a wire tray on the end of the reception counter below it. Left of center, a reception desk with a computer and neat color-coded folders, an empty office chair behind it, and above it on the wall a framed poster of storefront photographs. In the center, a shelf of thick black binders behind the desk. Right of center, an open door into a director's office with a desk and a blue binder. At the far right, a short hallway to a closed corner-office door with cut yellow police tape hanging from its frame. Worn carpet, radiators, fluorescent ceiling panels, a coat rack.

A small corner office of a charity's controller in an old brick building, after a police search, a gray November afternoon in 2018. On the left, a tall wooden bookshelf: binders and accounting reference books on the upper shelves, among them one thick old book in a worn faded green dust jacket; on the carpet beside the lower shelf, books stacked where they were pulled out. Upper left, a corner window over a rear alley and parking lot. In the center, a wooden desk with a paper desk-pad calendar, its center drawer hanging open with a broken lock, pens and stamps spilled on the blotter, and a clean empty rectangle in the dust on the right-hand corner where a heavy ornament stood; on the wall above it a framed newspaper photograph. Right of center, a gray four-drawer steel filing cabinet with its top two drawers open and black fingerprint powder on the handles, a gray-black toner stain on the carpet in front of it with a square cut out. At the far right, a small laser printer on a side table with pages in its tray, and the open office door with cut police tape. No people.

The spare room of a modest frame house used as a home office, a gray November afternoon in 2018, empty for days. On the left, a window onto a quiet street of small houses with porches and bare maples. In the center, a plain wooden desk with a lamp, an old mechanical adding machine and a brown accordion file squared to the edge, its top drawer closed. On the wall above the desk, framed photographs. On the right, a doorway into a small kitchen with unopened mail on the counter. Braided rug, a tidy single bed with a quilt, warm lamplight against gray daylight.

A graduate student's small apartment in a brick duplex in Squirrel Hill, Pittsburgh, a cold November afternoon in 2018. On the left, a desk by the window with a laptop, a lamp and stacks of course readers. In the center, open floor space before a worn couch with a folded blanket. On the right, a small kitchen with a refrigerator covered in magnets and photos, and a tall window onto a residential street with bare oaks. Bookshelves of policy books, a string of warm lights, a radiator.

A one-man maintenance contractor's garage bay and office beside a state highway in a small Pennsylvania town, an overcast November day in 2018. On the left, a clipboard hanging on a nail by an office door, and a shelf with a carbon-copy invoice book. In the center, a long wooden workbench with a pegboard of pipe wrenches, a vise, and an empty canvas tool bag hanging from a hook. Center right, a steel desk under a supply-house calendar with a bank statement on the blotter, and a plastic mail tray beside it. At the right, a wide open bay door onto a gravel lot. Concrete floor with oil stains, an overhead heater, a portable radio.

A small-town police detective bureau in an older civic building, November 2018. On the left, a whiteboard with a floor plan and photos pinned to it. In the center, open floor space in front of a row of desks. On the right, a window with blinds over a street and a stone county courthouse, and below it a cluttered detective's desk with binders, a monitor and a coffee mug. Fluorescent lights, filing cabinets, a bulletin board of notices.

A small accounting firm's partner's office on the fourth floor of an older downtown Pittsburgh building, a rainy November afternoon in 2018. On the left, floor-to-ceiling shelves of thick tax code volumes and client binders. In the center, open floor space before a desk with two monitors. Center right, a small round conference table with two chairs, a legal pad and two pens laid square. On the right, a tall window over Grant Street with office towers in the rain. Warm desk lamp, framed CPA certificates.

A polished financial advisory suite on the twenty-second floor of a downtown Pittsburgh office tower, a gray November day in 2018. On the left, a glass entry door with two brushed-steel nameplates mounted beside it, one above the other, the upper reading exactly HOLT ADVISORY LLC and the lower reading exactly MERIDIAN ADVISORY GROUP, and a curved walnut reception desk with a small nameplate. In the center, open floor space before a large executive desk with a leather out tray and a coffee cup on its corner. On the right, a wall of floor-to-ceiling windows over the rivers and the North Shore stadiums. Leather chairs, abstract art, low expensive lighting.

The small rear parking lot and service entrance of an old four-story brick office building, on a narrow brick alley in a small western Pennsylvania town, a cold gray November dusk in 2018. On the left, two green dumpsters against the back wall with a wide empty stretch of asphalt beside them. Left of center, a steel rear service door with a card reader beside it, its little light red, and through a glass panel beside it a lit security desk with an empty chair. On the right, across the alley, a bank's drive-through lane with a security camera on a tall pole pointed toward the lot. In the foreground right, the wet brick alley running off toward a side street, a few houses at its far end. Sodium lights coming on. No readable signs.
A manila private investigator's case folder, closed, with a printed label on the tab reading exactly: KELLER, M., a police photograph and a few typed pages sticking out of the side.

A white 2015 Ford Transit 250 high-roof work van seen from the side three-quarter angle, a black ladder rack on the roof, blue vinyl lettering on its side reading exactly: REDDICK MAINTENANCE. A Pennsylvania license plate with soft, unreadable characters.
A slate blue county crime laboratory folder, closed, with a white label on the front reading exactly: LAB REPORT.
A plain buff file folder with a typed white label on the front reading exactly: FINAL REPORT.
A stiff white courier envelope, sealed, with a neatly typed address label and a small printed return address in the corner, all soft and unreadable, lying flat at a slight angle.

The same stiff white courier envelope, opened along the top, a sheet of heavy cream letterhead and a photocopied page with a small slip stapled to its corner sliding out, the writing soft and unreadable.

A manila nine-by-twelve envelope from an accounting firm, flap tucked in, a few pages of spreadsheet schedules with soft, unreadable columns of figures showing at the top, a yellow sticky note on the front.

A police incident report on a clipboard: several typed pages with a Carroway Police Department header, a case number and soft, unreadable text, with a handwritten note in blue ink at the bottom of the last page.

Four glossy color crime scene photographs fanned out on a gray desk: a small office in disarray with a desk chair pushed back, a steel filing cabinet with two drawers open, a fan of black toner powder on carpet with a partial boot-sole print in it beside a photo scale, and a desk with a forced drawer. No body is visible in any photograph.

A medical examiner's typed summary on county letterhead, a single page with soft, unreadable text and a simple outline diagram of a head with a small triangular mark on its left side, on a steel table.

The corner of a wooden office desk in raking lamplight: a clean, dust-free rectangle about four by six inches in a fine film of dust where a heavy ornament stood, and above it on the wall a framed newspaper clipping of a smiling man in a tie holding a brass eagle on a walnut base.
An open drawer of a gray steel filing cabinet, green hanging files in a row with typed tabs, and one empty hanging folder pushed apart from the others, its tab reading exactly: FUND 2018 - WORKING.
A printed building access control report on continuous printer paper, columns of times and card numbers, soft and unreadable except two lines highlighted in yellow marker.
A county crime laboratory report beside a pair of well-worn tan leather work boots, one boot turned over to show a chevron lug sole with a worn outer heel edge, an evidence tag tied to its laces.
A typed police canvass statement form, a single page with a signature, soft unreadable text, a dog's leash lying across the corner of the page.
A paper desk-pad calendar for November 2018 covered in neat blue handwriting in the day squares, soft and unreadable, one Friday square underlined twice, pens and a rubber stamp scattered across it.
A printed email on a desk, soft unreadable text, a few lines bracketed in pencil, beside a pair of reading glasses.

An old thick hardback book with a worn, faded green dust jacket lying open, the jacket slipped off to reveal a slim green clothbound columnar ledger hidden inside in place of the book's boards, its ruled pages filled with neat columns of handwritten figures in pencil and ink, soft and unreadable.

A brown accordion file with a handwritten label reading exactly: HOME COPIES, stuffed with photocopied payment vouchers stamped with red approval stamps, yellow sticky notes in neat handwriting stuck to several, soft and unreadable.
Four printed pages lying in the output tray of a small laser printer, the top page headed DRAFT in bold, the rest soft and unreadable, a handwritten note in the margin of the last page.
A sealed white envelope with a name handwritten on it in blue ink, soft and unreadable, lying in an open wooden desk drawer among sorted pencils and a box of staples.
A printed nonprofit grant register, long tables of soft, unreadable names and dollar amounts, three lines near the bottom circled in red pen.
A thick black ring binder lying open, a payment request form with a second invoice clipped behind it, soft and unreadable, a paper clip catching the light.
A printed state business filing certificate with an official seal, soft and unreadable typed fields, and a yellow sticky note in a neat old man's handwriting stuck to the corner.

A blue three-ring binder open to a stack of identical disbursement authorization forms, each with the same flowing signature at the bottom, two forms side by side with the same date, the text soft and unreadable.
A printed online banking payment confirmation on a leather desk tray, a coffee cup's ring stain on the page, two words scrawled in black pen on the corner, the printed text soft and unreadable.
A bound contract with a cover page and a yellow plastic tab flag sticking out of one page, open to a dense page of numbered legal clauses, soft and unreadable.

A clipboard with a handwritten weekly job sheet in heavy block capitals, soft and unreadable, one word at the end of a line written in noticeably darker, heavier pen, a carpenter's pencil clipped beside it.
A white plastic building access card on a lanyard, a small printed credential record form beneath it with soft unreadable text and a handwritten note at the bottom.

Three grainy black-and-white security camera stills from above a bank drive-through lane at night: a white high-roof work van with a ladder rack in a small parking lot by two dumpsters, a lone figure carrying a bag toward a steel door, the van leaving. A vehicle registration printout beside them, soft and unreadable.
A small business bank statement on a cluttered steel desk, columns of small deposits soft and unreadable, one larger line highlighted, beside a coffee ring and a parts catalog.
A cell phone bill's call detail page, rows of times and phone numbers soft and unreadable, several rows highlighted in yellow, lying in a plastic mail tray.
A typed one-page witness statement with a handwritten signature at the bottom, soft and unreadable, beside a lanyard with an office key card.
Two printed emails stapled together, soft and unreadable, with a yellow Post-it note on top bearing a short handwritten line in looping script.
A typed letter on a nonprofit's letterhead with a pink While You Were Out phone message slip stapled behind it, the slip filled in by hand, all soft and unreadable.

A neat accountant's spreadsheet schedule printed on landscape paper, three blocks of figures with arrows all pointing to the same column on the right, a short handwritten note at the bottom, soft and unreadable.

A letter on heavy cream letterhead with an elegant engraved heading, written in a graceful hand, soft and unreadable, beside a photocopied invoice with a faint line of small gray print along its bottom edge and a courier waybill stapled to its corner.

Western Pennsylvania from the edge of Pittsburgh to a small county seat an hour to the east. On the left third, a dense city grid where two broad pale blue rivers meet to form a third, with bridges and a wooded neighborhood of small blocks just east of downtown. A highway in ochre runs from the city across the center through green rolling hills and farmland to the right third, where a small town sits: a compact downtown grid of a few blocks with a courthouse square, a residential grid of small streets below it, and a state highway running out east past a few commercial lots. Wooded hillsides and creeks fill the gaps.

Standing with his hands on his hips, a coffee mug hooked on one finger.
Standing with his hands loosely clasped in front of him, overcoat open.

The main truck gate of a Baltimore container terminal off Broening Highway, a cold rainy December morning in 2018. On the left, a steel and glass guard booth between inbound lanes with barrier arms. Left of center, a newer green sign on a pole by the gate with soft, unreadable lettering and an arrow pointing down a long fence line. In the center, open wet asphalt in front of a queue of semi-truck day cabs pulling container chassis, idling back along a service road. On the right, across the road, a double-wide trailer used as a union hall, a black ribbon on its porch rail. Floodlight poles, gantry cranes faint in the mist behind, puddles. No readable signs.

A fenced export container staging area on a Baltimore port terminal, a wet gray December afternoon in 2018. On the left, a chain-link pedestrian gate with a badge reader on a post, and a chained vehicle gate beyond. Left of center, a narrow asphalt lane between two rows of stacked shipping containers, with a dark stain on the asphalt and yellow police tape strung across the end of the lane between container corners. In the center, a tall stack of six folded steel flat racks against the north fence, and a concrete pad in front of it with a black grease smear under a small clear plastic tent and a yellow evidence marker. On the right, a chain-link lashing gear cage at the end of a container row, a wall rack of identical steel bars visible inside. Sodium floodlights, rain-wet steel, cranes in the mist. No people.

A small cargo verification office on the second floor of a port gate building, a gray December morning in 2018. On the left, a tall window looking down on truck lanes and a guard booth, with a cleared desk below it holding only a wire tray. In the center, open floor space before a second desk with a computer and stacks of shipping paperwork. Right of center, a plastic out tray at the end of that desk. On the right, a shared desk with a monitor showing a gray grid of numbers. Fluorescent lights, a wall calendar, safety posters, hi-vis vests on hooks. No readable text.

Inside a steel lashing gear shed beside a container staging area, a cold wet December day in 2018. On the left, a steel door with a badge reader and a clipboard hanging on a hook beside it. Left of center, a scarred steel workbench with a vise, a grease gun and a radio. In the center, tall racks of coiled chain, crates of container twistlocks and hanging load binders. On the right, a row of gray steel gear lockers with stenciled names, one of them, left of the rest, with its own combination padlock. Corrugated walls, a single caged work light, wet concrete floor. No people. No readable text.

A port terminal security office beside the main gate, a rainy December day in 2018. On the left, a workstation with a computer and a small printer. Left of center, a shelf holding thick black binders. In the center and right, a desk under a wall of security monitors showing camera views of gates, container stacks and lanes, a folder of printed stills on the desk. At the far right, a narrow window looking out on a guard booth and a truck queue in the rain. Fluorescent lights, a coffee maker, radios charging. No people. No readable text.

The front room and kitchen of a small brick rowhouse in Highlandtown, East Baltimore, a gray December afternoon in 2018. On the left, a wall of framed family photographs above a radiator. Left of center, open floor space before a worn couch with a child's backpack on it. In the center, a doorway into a narrow kitchen with a refrigerator covered in a child's drawings. On the right, through an open doorway into a small back room, a little desk wedged beside a washing machine, with a home printer and a coffee mug on a folded sheet of paper. Lace curtains, a crucifix, warm lamplight against gray daylight. No people.

A port terminal operations supervisor's office in an administration building, a gray December day in 2018. On the left, a shelf of blue ring binders. In the center, open floor space before a large desk with a desk phone, a monitor and a closed drawer. On the wall above the desk, framed photographs including an aerial view of a container terminal. Right of center, a two-drawer steel file cabinet behind the desk. On the far right, a window looking out over cranes on a quay and container stacks in the rain. Fluorescent lights, a hard hat on a filing cabinet. No people. No readable text.

The president's office of a logistics and security company in a converted brick warehouse in Canton, Baltimore, a gray December afternoon in 2018. On the left, a lateral file cabinet by the door. In the center, open floor space before a large walnut desk, framed photographs of green semi-trucks on the brick wall behind it. Right of center, a low walnut credenza with closed locked doors behind the desk. On the right, open floor space below a wide warehouse window looking out on Clinton Street and the harbor cranes beyond. Exposed beams, leather chairs, expensive and quiet. No people. No readable text.

The same converted brick warehouse office in Canton, Baltimore, during a police search on a December evening in 2018. On the left, a lateral file cabinet by the door with its drawers open and evidence tape across them. In the center, open floor space before a large walnut desk cleared of papers, framed photographs of green semi-trucks on the brick wall behind it. Right of center, a walnut credenza with its doors open and its lock drilled out, folders inside. On the right, a hand truck stacked with cardboard evidence boxes below a wide warehouse window, harbor lights beyond. Harsh overhead light. No people. No readable text.

Inside an office trailer at a small private security company's fenced yard in Curtis Bay, Baltimore, a raw gray December day in 2018. On the left, a whiteboard on the paneled wall with a printed weekly schedule taped to it and a clipboard beside it. Left of center, a metal desk with two-way radios charging and a stack of forms. In the center, open floor space. On the right, an open trailer door looking out on a gravel yard behind a chain-link fence, where a gray heavy-duty pickup truck is parked nose-out. A space heater, a coffee maker, a calendar. No people. No readable text.

An accounts payable office on the first floor of a port terminal administration building, a rainy December afternoon in 2018. On the left, a shelf of thick contract binders behind a counter. In the center, open floor space before a tidy desk with a printed ledger and a calculator. On the wall center, a framed certificate. On the right, a window looking out on a wet employee parking lot and container stacks beyond. Fluorescent lights, gray cubicle panels, a copier. No people. No readable text.

A big-city police homicide unit squad room in Baltimore, December 2018. On the left, a whiteboard with a case number, a terminal map and photos. In the center, open floor space in front of a row of cluttered detective desks. Center right, a desk with case files stacked crosswise and a coffee cup. On the right, the wired-glass window of an interview room, lit inside, and at the far right a window with blinds over a downtown street in the rain. Fluorescent lights, filing cabinets. No people. No readable text.

A freight transload yard on the south shore of Baltimore's harbor in Fairfield, a raw gray December morning in 2018, with a police search under way. On the left, a small plywood gate shack with a window and a binder hanging on a nail. Left of center, a long corrugated steel shed with three numbered roll-up bay doors, the third one open on a loading dock. On the right, the open door of a cramped site office: a gray steel file cabinet with its drawers drilled open, a plain steel desk with a radio, and a rubber desk mat rolled back from a steel floor safe set flush into the concrete floor. Puddles, a forklift, police tape, the harbor and cranes beyond. No people. No readable signs.
A manila private investigator's case folder, closed, with a printed label on the tab reading exactly: NAVARRO, H., a police photograph and a few typed fax pages sticking out of the side.

A gray 2016 Ford F-250 Super Duty crew cab pickup seen from the side three-quarter angle, an amber LED light bar across the roof, white vinyl lettering on the front door reading exactly: FISK FREIGHT SECURITY. A Maryland license plate with soft, unreadable characters.
A slate blue police laboratory folder, closed, with a white label on the front reading exactly: LAB REPORT.
A plain buff file folder with a typed white label on the front reading exactly: FINAL REPORT.
A stiff white and red courier envelope, sealed, with a printed address label and a clear plastic waybill pocket, the writing soft and unreadable, no return address, lying flat at a slight angle.
The same courier envelope, opened along the top, a thick sheaf of photocopied pages and a thin courier waybill slip sliding out, the writing soft and unreadable.
A tan interoffice envelope with a string-and-button closure and a yellow sticky note on the front, a few typed pages showing at the top, the writing soft and unreadable.

Two plainclothes police detectives in dark jackets and an agent in a navy windbreaker with no readable words, standing beside a hand truck stacked with cardboard evidence boxes, one photographing an open folder.
A steel floor safe set into a concrete floor, its heavy door standing open, bundles of banded cash, a passport and a clear plastic sleeve with a single typed page inside.

A gray steel gear locker standing open: a spare hi-vis vest and a hard hat on a hook, a coil of chain on the shelf, and a paper drugstore photo envelope tucked into the vent slots on the inside of the door, an open combination padlock hanging from the hasp.
A black hardback notebook half wrapped in a greasy blue shop rag, lying under a coil of steel lashing chain.

A police incident report on a clipboard: several typed pages with a Baltimore Police Department header, a case number and soft, unreadable text, with a handwritten note in blue ink at the bottom of the last page.

Five glossy color crime scene photographs fanned out on a gray desk: a north fence behind a stack of folded steel flat racks, a dark stain on wet asphalt between container rows, an open wallet and an upended lunch cooler, a chain-link cage with a rack of steel bars, and a black grease smear with a yellow marker. No body is visible in any photograph.
A medical examiner's summary of findings: two typed pages with a state seal at the top and soft, unreadable text, and a simple outline diagram of a human head with a small marked area on one side.
A heavy steel binder bar about three feet long with one end bent into a hook, lying in a clear evidence bag with a red evidence tag, beside a typed laboratory report with soft, unreadable text.
A close photograph of a black grease smear on concrete with the front half of a lugged work boot sole print in it, a yellow evidence marker and a photo scale beside it.
A smartphone screen showing a message thread and a call log with soft, unreadable text, beside a printed screenshot of a map with a single gray location dot near a harbor.
A printed access control report on plain paper: a short list of time stamps and badge numbers in columns, the text soft and unreadable.
A typed police canvass statement, two pages stapled, with a signature at the bottom and soft, unreadable text.
A black hardback notebook lying open, pages of handwritten block capitals and numbers, soft and unreadable, a greasy blue shop rag beside it.

A paper drugstore photo envelope with a stack of glossy prints spilling out: close photographs of numbered steel container seals, a digital load display, and a night photograph of a semi-truck under gate floodlights, handwriting on the backs of some prints.
A paper dock receipt form in a red folder, filled in by hand and signed, with a yellow sticky note clipped to the top, the writing soft and unreadable.
A printout from a terminal computer system, a dense grid of fields and numbers, face down, with a small sticky note in handwriting on it, the text soft and unreadable.
A blue ring binder lying open to printed daily schedule sheets with columns of times and numbers, a line of handwriting in blue ink at the foot of a sheet, the text soft and unreadable.
A printed email folded in thirds and opened flat, a coffee ring on one corner, a short handwritten note across the top, the text soft and unreadable.
A manila personnel folder lying open to a printed email with a red rubber stamp and initials, the text soft and unreadable.
A clipboard holding two printed sheets: a door reader printout of times and a gear locker roster, the text soft and unreadable.
A printed weekly schedule grid taped to a whiteboard, with a sign-in sheet on a bulldog clip beside it, names and times in handwriting, soft and unreadable.
A contractor credential record page in a plastic sleeve, typed fields and a small ID photo, with a handwritten margin note, the text soft and unreadable.
A motor vehicle registration printout beside an insurer's photograph of a gray heavy-duty pickup truck with an amber light bar on its roof and lettering on its door, the text soft and unreadable.
An online banking printout of a business checking account, columns of dates and amounts, under a black stapler, the text soft and unreadable.

Several pages of telephone call detail records with columns of numbers, times and cell site codes, a few lines highlighted in yellow and a handwritten note in the margin, the text soft and unreadable.
A thick sheaf of photocopied contract pages, slightly gray from the copier, with a thin courier waybill slip on top, the text soft and unreadable.
A smartphone held out across a desk, its screen showing a text message conversation, the words soft and unreadable.
A two-page annual ethics and financial disclosure form with checkboxes and a signature, a pension statement clipped behind it, the text soft and unreadable.
A typed witness statement, two pages, signed at the bottom, the text soft and unreadable.
A trucker's paper log book lying open, grid pages filled in by hand with handwritten notes in the margins, the text soft and unreadable.
Four grainy black and white security camera stills of a gate lane at night in the rain: a box truck, a heavy-duty pickup with a roof light bar, a patrol SUV, and the same pickup leaving.
A typed police search warrant return and digital extraction summary, several pages, beside an iPhone with a cracked corner sealed in a clear evidence bag with a red tag.
A single-page company invoice with a letterhead, line items and a total, a remit-to box and an approval initial, the text soft and unreadable.
State articles of organization for a limited liability company, an official form with a filing stamp, the text soft and unreadable.
A printed accounting ledger page with one line highlighted in yellow and a pencil note beside it, the text soft and unreadable.
A one-page business letter on a consultant's letterhead, signed in blue ink, with a tax form attached behind it, the text soft and unreadable.
A manila folder lying open to a typed five-page report with a restricted header, and a note scrawled across the top in black felt pen, the text soft and unreadable.
A contract amendment, several typed pages stapled at the corner, signatures at the bottom, a yellow sticky tab on one page, the text soft and unreadable.
A swollen three-ring binder lying open to handwritten log pages in several different hands, columns of times and numbers with initials, the text soft and unreadable.
A printed spreadsheet table of eight rows with columns of numbers and a handwritten note at the bottom, the text soft and unreadable.
Two printed pages of a client register, a line circled in pen with a handwritten note beside it, the text soft and unreadable.
A typed police financial schedule, columns of receipts and payments with totals, a handwritten note at the foot, the text soft and unreadable.
A single typed page with no letterhead and a short handwritten line at the bottom, the text soft and unreadable.
A single typed sheet in a clear plastic sleeve with no letterhead and no signature, a yellow sticky note stuck to the sleeve, the text soft and unreadable.

Baltimore's harbor seen from above, the broad pale blue Patapsco River running from the inner harbor at the top center out to the right toward the bay. On the north shore, a dense downtown grid at the top center, rowhouse neighborhoods of small blocks to its east, an old waterfront warehouse district along the water, and further east and south along the north shore a large container terminal: long piers, cranes, rows of stacked containers and a fenced staging area. On the south shore, an industrial district of rail yards, a transload yard by the water and fenced lots in a bay further south. In the far upper left corner, a highway in ochre running off the edge of the sheet to the west, toward distant green hills.
images.suffix: A hand-painted street map, seen flat from directly above and filling the whole image edge to edge like a sheet laid on a table: no table, no border, no frame. Muted map colors: cream paper, ochre streets, sage green parkland, pale blue water, faint fold creases. Absolutely no words, letters, numbers, street names or symbols anywhere on the map.

images.subject: The marble lobby of a grand old Park Avenue hotel in Manhattan late on a December night in 2018, during an interrupted charity gala. On the far left, a brass easel holding a framed gala sign beside tall gilded ballroom doors. Left of center, open marble floor before two columns and a bench. In the center, a long framed seating chart on an easel, and below it the tall double doors to the ballroom, standing open. Right of center, open floor before a door marked EVENT OFFICE. On the right, a plain door to the security office behind the front desk, a revolving door onto the avenue with police lights glowing blue outside, and a long marble front desk under a gilt clock. Christmas garlands, warm chandelier light.

A grand hotel ballroom during a charity gala that has just been stopped, December 2018. On the left, tall framed photograph panels of charity programs along the wall, and open floor before them. At the top center, a low stage hung with deep blue velvet with a lectern and an auctioneer's stand. In the center and below, round tables with white cloths, candles and flowers, one near the stage with an untouched dessert and a gray wrap over a chair back. Right of center, open floor between tables. On the right, a carpeted staircase rising to a mezzanine behind service screens, and the tall doors back to the lobby. Chandeliers, warm gold light, half-empty champagne glasses.

The same grand hotel ballroom the morning after a gala, December 2018, being cleared. On the left, the framed charity photograph panels still along the wall. At the top center, the stage stripped of its velvet, a man on a ladder taking down lights. In the center, round tables stripped to bare wood, chairs stacked on dollies, a neat stack of place cards on one table. On the right, the carpeted staircase to the mezzanine and the tall doors to the lobby. Pale daylight from high windows, work lights, no party left.

A carpeted hotel mezzanine conference corridor at night, December 2018. At the top left, a small black security camera dome on the ceiling above the top of a staircase landing; at the left, the stair landing going down. Left of center, a swinging pantry door with a porthole window. In the center, a row of walnut doors with brass card readers and small engraved letter plates, one door in the middle ajar with light inside. Upper right of center, a second camera dome on the ceiling, turned toward the far end. On the right, a plain staff door at the far end with evidence tape across its upper jamb, and beside it a window bay with two armchairs and a potted palm overlooking a lit avenue.

A small private hotel conference suite after a death, a crime scene at night, December 2018. On the left, a long walnut credenza against the wall under a framed engraving of Grand Central, with one green marble bookend at its right end and a row of display books fallen flat. In the center, a walnut conference table for eight with a cocktail tray: a crystal decanter and two tumblers, one standing with whiskey in it. Below the table, open carpet. Right of center, a leather chair lying overturned and a small side table with its drawer pulled out. On the right, the suite door, with a numbered yellow evidence tent on the carpet just inside it. Low lamplight, a crime scene photographer's light stand in a corner.

A cramped hotel security office behind the front desk, night, December 2018. On the left, a wall of sixteen surveillance monitors in a grid showing a lobby, a loading dock and corridors. In the center, open floor before a desk with a keyboard and a radio charger. Right of center, a small credential card printer beside a box of blank cards and a ring binder. On the right, a door back to the lobby. Fluorescent light, a coffee mug, clipboards on hooks.

The back of house of a big Manhattan hotel: a concrete service corridor ending at a loading dock, December 2018. On the left, a plain staff door into the corridor. Left of center, open floor before the scuffed steel doors of a service elevator with a card reader. In the center, a steel dock desk with a clipboard and a space heater beside a roll-up door. On the right, the half-open dock door onto a small gated vendor lot with a florist's van and a linen truck and a plate reader camera on the gatepost. Fluorescent tubes, banquet carts, cold gray daylight.

The reception hall of a private foundation in an old Fifth Avenue mansion in Manhattan, a gray December day in 2018. On the left, glass-fronted shelves of matching blue annual reports. Left of center, open parquet floor. In the center, through open double doors at the top, a refined office with a Hudson River painting over a fireplace and an empty desk. Right of center, open floor, and a small side office with binders and two monitors. On the right, a carved wooden door to a stair going down. Persian rugs, flowers, soft lamplight.

A basement records archive under an old Manhattan building, December 2018. On the left, steel shelving with gray archive boxes, one labeled box on a bottom shelf. Left of center, shelves of black binders. In the center, a tall steel filing cabinet of tax files. Right of center, a row of binders by year on a shelf. On the right, a narrow stair going back up. Fluorescent tubes, a dehumidifier, concrete floor.

A small independent investment adviser's office on a high floor of a Sixth Avenue tower in Manhattan, a gray December day in 2018. On the left, a tilting wooden drafting board by a tall window with a sheet of graph paper taped to it. Left of center, open floor. In the center, a plain oak desk with a green-shaded lamp and a fountain pen tray. Above the desk, a framed old university diploma on the wall. On the right, full bookshelves of investment books and bound annual reports, and a photograph of a couple on a sailboat.

A prewar apartment on the Upper West Side of Manhattan on a gray winter afternoon in 2018. On the left, a tall window onto brownstone stoops and bare ginkgo trees. Left of center, open floor before a sofa. In the center, through an open door, a small study with a desk and a single sheet of paper squared on the blotter. Right of center, an upright piano with framed photographs. On the right, a hall closet door ajar with an overcoat and umbrella. Books everywhere, a radiator, warm lamps.

A sleek corner law office high in a Lexington Avenue tower in Manhattan, December 2018. On the left, a white marble reception counter with one orchid, and a paralegal's desk behind it. Left of center, open floor. In the center, tall windows with the Chrysler Building close by, and below them a glass desk with a leather-bound book on it. Right of center, a locked walnut credenza behind the desk. On the right, a wall of framed diplomas and photographs. Cool gray daylight, polished and spare.

A small private security firm's office on the second floor over a tire shop on a Queens boulevard, a rainy December day in 2018. On the left, a door with a clipboard hanging on a hook beside it. Left of center, open floor. In the center, a wall rack of handheld radios in chargers with green lights, and below it a metal desk with a laptop and radio chargers. Right of center, a two-drawer steel file cabinet. On the right, a window onto elevated subway tracks and the Manhattan skyline across the river. Fluorescent light, a framed military photograph, equipment cases.

A corporate services office in a Madison Avenue building in Manhattan, December 2018. On the left, a front desk with a phone and a visitor log. In the center at the top, a wall of two hundred small brass mail slots with tiny company nameplates, soft and unreadable. In the center below, a long counter with three binders laid out on it. On the right, a window onto Madison Avenue with buses in the slush. Beige carpet, fluorescent light, impersonal.

A New York City police detective squad room in 2018. On the left, a whiteboard with a case number, a hotel floor plan and a photograph pinned to it. Left of center, open floor in front of a row of desks. In the center, a detective's desk with case folders, a monitor and a takeout coffee cup. Right of center, a glass-walled interview room with a table and two chairs. On the right, a wire-glass window and a radiator. Fluorescent light, filing cabinets, a bulletin board of notices.
Courteous and a little reserved, at a charity dinner.

images.subject: The lobby of an upscale downtown Washington, D.C. hotel near Thomas Circle on a sleety November afternoon in 2018, Thanksgiving week. Left of center, a long marble front desk with computer screens, an empty sofa by a tall window in front of it, and a smoked-glass camera dome in the ceiling above the desk. In the center, a round table with a tall arrangement of rust and gold chrysanthemums and wheat stalks, and behind it an open stretch of marble floor. Right of center, above head height, a discreet door marked only by a small plaque, and a polished wooden door to the general manager's office. On the right, a bank of brass guest elevators. At the far right, a valet podium with a board of numbered key hooks by a passage to a garage ramp. Luggage carts, warm lamplight, coffered ceiling.

A long, straight hotel guest corridor on the sixth floor, seen from the elevator landing, Washington, D.C., 2018. On the left, the brass doors of the guest elevators and, high on the ceiling just ahead, a smoked-glass camera dome. Patterned carpet and brass sconces lead away down the corridor in strong perspective, numbered room doors on both sides. Right of center, a room door with a paper Do Not Disturb card on its handle, and next to it the door of Room 614. At the far end of the corridor, brightly lit: a small ice-machine alcove and, under a lit green EXIT sign, a plain gray steel service door flush with the wall with a card reader and a small keypad beside it. Quiet, evening light.

styles.c002: Painted noir illustration in the manner of a 1980s paperback mystery cover and classic hand-painted point-and-click adventure game backgrounds.
